title: Equivariant resolution of one split marked nodal curve over a smooth pair
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $S$ an integral finite-type $F$-scheme, and $D\subseteq S$ a closed subset [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $f:T\to S$ be projective, flat and finitely presented [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty connected reduced one-dimensional nodal geometric fibres [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres] and smooth geometrically integral generic fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Nodal means that the completed geometric local ring at a nonsmooth point is $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$. Assume $f$ is smooth over $S\setminus D$, and let $M$ be a finite disjoint union of sections in its relative smooth locus [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let a finite group $J$ act on $F,T,S$ compatibly with $f$, preserving $D$ and $M$. Assume the marked nodal curve is split: fibre components, nodes and two branches descend to the residue field, and point stabilizers in $S$ act trivially on the fibre dual graph with marked legs. Let $t:S_0\to S$ be an equivariant projective birational surjection, where $S_0$ is integral and smooth over $F$ and the reduced inverse image of $D$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor $E$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. There is a $J$-equivariant projective birational surjection $r:T'\to T\times_SS_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with $T'$ integral and smooth over $F$. The composite $T'\to T$ is also projective birational and surjective. The map $r$ is an isomorphism outside the pullback of $|M|\cup f^{-1}D$, and the reduced inverse image of that closed set is a relative strict normal crossings divisor $E'$ on $T'/F$. Every local ring of $T'$ is regular, and the components of $E'$ through a point have local equations which are distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-regular-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. If $S_0$ is projective over $F$ in the finite-projective-space convention, $T'$ is projective over $F$ in that convention [def-kun-projective]. Birational means an isomorphism between dense opens and equality of function fields. Empty $D$ and $M$ are allowed. The case $t=\mathrm{id}$ includes resolution of a marked nodal curve directly over a smooth SNC pair.

proof.text: Put $W=T\times_SS_0$, $g:W\to S_0$, $q:W\to T$, $M_0=M\times_SS_0$ and $B=|M_0|\cup g^{-1}|E|$. The marked nodal base-change geometry lemma gives integral Noetherian finite-type $T,W$, the required nodal and marking hypotheses for $g$, projectivity of $g,q$, and birational surjectivity of $q$. Its diagonal action preserves $B$.

source.place: X Lemma 2.2 proof, p.149, base modification of one marked nodal curve; Stacks Tags 02V6, morphisms.tex lemma-base-change-projective, and 0C5B, curves.tex lemma-base-change-nodal-family; elementary flat generic-fibre integrality calculation in returned steps 1--3 and the base-change part of step 15.

proof.text: Apply the marked nodal log-chart lemma to $g$, the given smooth pair $(S_0,E)$ and $M_0$. Thus $U=W\setminus B$ is dense, $(W,B)$ is fs log regular and log smooth over the trivial log field $F$. Its boundary is exactly the pullback support of $|M|\cup f^{-1}D$.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 and proof, pp.70--71, including its logarithmic smoothness assertion and cocartesian monoid chart; X Lemma 2.2 p.149 smooth-pair-over-a-field remark. Returned steps 4--6.

proof.text: Apply equivariant log-smooth fan regularization to $(W,B)$, obtaining $a:W_1\to W$ projective birational and equivariant, isomorphic over $U$, with $W_1$ integral and smooth over $F$ and $B_1=(a^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$ having smooth relative coordinate normal crossings charts.

source.place: VIII 3.3.13--3.3.15 and 3.4.4--3.4.9, pp.108--112, and 4.1.1 p.117; X Lemma 2.2 p.149 smooth-pair-over-a-field refinement. Returned steps 7--9: strict fan descent, normalized blowup projectivity, and free-characteristic relative charts.

proof.text: Apply relative maximal-branch strictification to $(W_1,B_1)$. It gives $b:T\prime\to W_1$, projective birational and equivariant, isomorphic off $B_1$, with $T\prime$ integral regular and smooth over $F$, and $E\prime=(b^{-1}B_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$ relative strict normal crossings.

source.place: VIII 4.1.2--4.1.8 pp.117--118 and 4.2.8--4.2.9 pp.120--121, with the explicit coordinate calculation over F required by X Lemma 2.2 p.149. Returned steps 10--12.

proof.text: Set $r=ab$. Projective-bundle composition applies over the Noetherian targets $W,T,S_0$ and makes $r$, $qr$ and $gr$ projective. Both towers are isomorphisms over the same dense $U$; hence $r$ is birational and unchanged on $U$. It is closed by projective-bundle properness, so its image, containing dense $U$, is all of $W$. Since $q$ is birational surjective, so is $qr$. The lifted actions compose, and reduced total inverse images give $E\prime=(r^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$.

source.place: VIII 3.4.9 and 4.1.1--4.1.8; returned step 13 and base-change portion of step 15

proof.text: The strict-boundary parameter criterion gives $I_{E\prime,x}=(t_1\cdots t_s)$ in each ordinary regular local ring of $T\prime$. The regular-local factorization lemma makes the distinct $t_i$ prime, so the reduced components through $x$ have precisely the distinct ideals $(t_i)$, giving the asserted individual parameter equations.

source.place: VIII Remark 4.2.2(i); Stacks 0BI9 definition-strict-normal-crossings and 0BIA lemma-strict-normal-crossings; returned step 14

proof.text: If $S_0$ is H-projective over $F$, its projective-space embedding supplies an ample invertible sheaf. Apply projective-bundle-to-H-projective to $gr:T\prime\to S_0$ and then H-projective composition with $S_0\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. This gives the last clause in the stated convention.

This answers the human's re-split note of 2026-10-21, released 13:47 on 2026-10-22, after the NC 680dd PASS and the Q19 stage-2 PASS. Compliance: the item statement is byte-identical to live; I checked by script that all 15 old step texts survive verbatim in the report; there are 4 new statement-only nodes of comparable size (old steps 1-3, 4-6, 7-9, 10-12); the parent is a 2237-character, 7-step assembly. Old steps 13-15 became parent steps 5-7 with all their clauses kept (the q-geometry part of 15 went into node A). No argument was dropped, and no node restates the item or a clause of it. All four nodes are true. (A) nodal-birational-base-change-geometry: C embeds in C⊗K by flatness, so T and W are integral (K(S0)=K(S)); inverse images of dense opens are dense; q is birational and surjective; projectivity is 02V6 base change. (B) marked-nodal-relative-log-charts matches ILO VI Prop 1.9, which I read in the pdftotext and which asserts log smoothness too. Its chart is R=Z×P with 1↦ε; I recomputed coker(R^gp→Q^gp)=Z²/(1,1)≅Z, torsion-free. The comparison scheme is uv=εα(a), and the definition of log smoothness allows a smooth comparison map. (C) equivariant-log-smooth-fan-regularization is ILO VIII 3.3.15/3.4.9 fan descent. Saturated log blowups are log étale; the underlying stages are normalized blowups (Bl_J)^ν, projective in the bundle sense; free characteristic monoids give smooth N^r charts by the relative NC criterion; equivariance comes from functoriality. (D) relative-nc-maximal-branch-strictification is ILO VIII 4.1.6-4.1.8. In charts the strict transform is ∏_{k≠j}v_k, so the maximum branch count drops; E and the strict transforms of H stay strict SNC; the m=1 case and B=∅ hold; there are at most m0 steps; centres are intrinsic and J-invariant. Parent hypotheses check node by node, with one small gap: step 4 leaves 'B1 effective Cartier' unstated. It is immediate, since B1 is étale-locally cut out by one nonzerodivisor (c is flat), and I accepted it. Steps 6-7 are unchanged base arguments. No duplicates: the candidates are either dropped lem-per resolution nodes (gabber-log-blowup-regularization, log-regular-projective-log-resolution, noetherian-log-pair-strict-resolution) or narrower trf nodes (normal-crossings-strictification needs an algebraically closed field; maximal-branch-blowup, permissible-boundary-preservation and monoidal-resolution-tower are single steps or give free monoids only; nodal-log-regularity has no log-smooth clause). No SGA source is used, and no node cited is missing or dropped. Batch-5: I accept all 16 flagged citations. def-trf-log-regular-pair, def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale, def-trf-fine-fan-blowup, def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism, def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor, def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres and def-trf-normal-crossings-branch-count are general definitions. lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup is general fan-chart log geometry. All were already in the item's closure through the old steps and its stmt_deps, and none is part of the trace formula, Poincaré duality or their proofs.
